messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: Error using ChoiceRT_ddm_single
parts:
Hello Zhenna,


I think that for the LBA_single model, you may be getting an error because the conditions start from 2 rather than 1. There is a loop in the code which assumes that conditions start at 1 (e.g. rawdata$condition = c(2,2,2,1,1,2,2,1,1,1) instead of rawdata$condition = c(3,3,3,2,2,3,3,2,2,2)), and this causes there to be 0 observations for one of the conditions. 


Of course, this is something that we can easily fix to avoid this sort of confusion in the future. For now, you should be able to get it to work if you subtract 1 from your condition vector and then save the data so that condition starts at 1. 


For the ddm_single, I think this is a problem with the subjID column having multiple IDs. The *_single models all assume that there is only a single subject. That said, we could change this if users are interested in fitting "fixed effects" models. 


When I ran your data through the ddm for multiple subjects, it looks like one of them (the 37th unique subject in the data) did not have any responses for one of the 2 choice options which is causing your error. If you remove subjects who only responded to a single option, you should be able to run the ddm over your data. From a pure modeling perspective, it is probably best to remove those subjects because it will be very difficult to estimate their parameters.   


These are great things to point out, and we can certainly make some better error-catching messages for cases like this. Thanks a lot for taking the time to post! 


Best,

Nate
